hist-ea-01-c3.text: Sue Gronewald, Asia for Educators, Columbia University. The Ming Voyages. Asia for Educators, Columbia University.
hist-ea-01-c3.quote: But for the three last voyages, Zheng went even further, all the way to the east coast of Africa.
hist-ea-01-c3.claim: Zheng He's massive treasure fleets sailed as far as Africa, and then the voyages were halted.

hist-ea-01-c3.text: Columbia University, Asia for Educators. Taiping Rebellion (1850-1864). Asia for Educators, Columbia University.
hist-ea-01-c3.quote: It is estimated that the entire rebellion cost more than twenty million lives (twice that of World War I).
hist-ea-01-c3.claim: the Taiping Rebellion, which left ~20 million dead.

hist-ea-01-c2.text: Daniel C. Waugh (quoting Richard B. Mather, foreword to Xiong, Sui-Tang Chang'an, 2000). Chang'an (Xian). Silk Road Seattle, University of Washington.
hist-ea-01-c2.quote: At the height of its glory in the mid-eighth century, Chang'an was the most populous, cosmopolitan, and civilized city in the world
hist-ea-01-c2.claim: Walk into Chang'an during the Tang dynasty (618-907) and you'd be in the world's largest city.

hist-ea-01-c1.text: Michael Tsin (1995). Annotated Timeline of Chinese History. Asia for Educators, Columbia University.
hist-ea-01-c1.quote: Confucianism was established as orthodoxy and open civil service examinations were introduced.
